description.narrative: Overall goal: The overall goal of this Project is more inclusive, effective, transparent and accountable governance of Liberia. This goal will be achieved through improved legal and regulatory frameworks, stronger public institutions, more engaged and responsible stakeholders, and peaceful electoral and democratic processes. As an overreaching goal, this electoral cycle will also enhance national ownership as well as continued progress towards peaceful, credible, inclusive and transparent electoral processes in Liberia. Expected results: Output 1: Inclusion and transparency of the electoral process is strengthened 1.1 NEC strategic approach to communication, external relations, and disinformation management 1.2 Strengthening capacity of NEC, civil society, and other actors in conducting civic and voter education 1.3 Improved access and opportunity of the right to vote to vulnerable groups Output 2: Institutional capacity and accountability of NEC and electoral stakeholders enhanced 2.1 Project's capacity-building support is based in detailed and realistic assessment at all levels 2.2 Technical Capacity and Skills of NEC at All Levels are strengthened 2.3 Enhanced technical capacity of electoral stakeholders towards greater accountability and electoral integrity 2.4 Increased Integrity and Sustainability of Electoral Operations, including Voter Registration Process 2.5: NEC Infrastructure Strengthening towards Greater Electoral Integrity Output 3: Conflict prevention and mitigation mechanisms to support peaceful conduct of elections are strengthened 3.1 Electoral security further improved 3.2 Awareness raised and mitigation measures implemented to mitigate Violence Against Women in Elections (VAWIE)

FN: s utvecklingsprogram (UNDP) har från Sida ansökt om 40 miljoner kronor för att finansiera insatsen Liberia Electoral Support Project (LESP) under 2021 - 2024. Insatsen bedöms vara i linje med de övergripande prioriteringarna och inriktningen för Sveriges Strategi för utvecklingsbistånd i Liberia 2021 - 2025.
Det övergripande målet för detta projekt är att fortsätta stärka valinstitutionerna- och processerna. Som ett övegripande mål bör denna cykel präglas av att ytterligare förstärka det nationellt ägandet och framsteg mot fredliga, trovärdiga, inkluderande och transparenta valprocesser i Liberia.
Den totala budgeten för LESP-projektets varaktighet är 16,180,764.00 miljoner USD. Vid tidpunkten för denna bedömning är det svenska bidraget 40.0 miljoner kronor, cirka 4,8 miljoner USD. UNDP:s planerade stöd från egna resurser är 1.5 miljoner USD. När det gäller andra externa givarresurser har EU visat ett intresse av att finansiera valprojektet med 15.0 miljoner EUR och Irland har uttryckt ett åtagande om 2.0 miljoner EUR.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has through Sida applied for funding of 40 million SEK to fund the Liberia Electoral Support Project (LESP) during 2021 - 2024. The contribution is assessed to be in line with the overarching priorities and direction of Swedish Strategy for Development cooperation in Liberia 2021 - 2025.
The overall objective of this Project is to continue strengthening the electoral institutions and processes. As an overreaching goal, this cycle should be marked by further enhanced national ownership as well as continued progress towards peaceful, credible, inclusive and transparent electoral processes in Liberia.
The total budget for the LESP project duration is USD 16,180,764.00 million. At the time of this appraisal, the Swedish contribution is SEK 40.0 million, approximately USD 4.8 million. UNDP core contribution is so far at USD 1.5 million. As for other external donor resources, the EU has indicated an interest to fund the elections project with EUR 15.0 million and Ireland has made a commitment of EUR 2.0 million.

description.narrative:
As stated in the last progress report, the following results were examples of achievements reached in 2024:
Area 1: Enhanced electoral cycle and sustenance of peace -A comprehensive series of post-election review activities were undertaken by the NEC and other stakeholders to identify good practices and lessons learned for the future. -NEC launched its Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) policy in July 2024, revised to include inclusion of persons with disabilities within the policy. -The iVerify Platform was formally handed over to Local Voices Liberia. -UNDP supported institutional development initiatives for the NEC including BRIDGE workshops and an institutional memory project to develop a digital archive structure. -Capacities of NEC (Assistant) Magistrates were strengthened in digital data collection tools and report procedures and applied in regular M&E reporting from the field. -Support was provided to boundary delimitation data management and spatial mapping technical activities, including preparation of census data together with LISGIS Political parties were trained in financial reporting and management resulting in improved annual financial reporting compliance. -Political parties were trained in financial reporting and management resulting in improved annual financial reporting compliance. -A curriculum on gender sensitive reporting for journalists is under development, with training delivered to journalists. -Support was provided to by-election activities through genderawareness activities with local leaders and conflict prevention dialogues.
Area 2: Enhanced participation of women and inclusion of marginalized groups in political processes -The Womens Legislative Caucus reviewed its Constitution, and developed and launched on 29 May a Strategic Plan for the period 2024-2028 -On 12 June, the Womens Legislative Caucus convened a meeting with the National Elections Commission to discuss the status of electoral reform and explore legal and collaborative pathways to advance gender-responsive provisions. -NIMD engaged NAYMOTE-Liberia in development of the curriculum for a Democracy School for youth of political parties and civil society. -Consultative meetings were held with political parties and their youth wings in preparation for intraparty and interparty dialogues. -The NEC and political parties revised the MoU establishing the IPCC framework, including strengthening provisions to promote inclusion, including for persons with disabilities. -The project conducted a series of county-based consultations with women and youth for development of issue-based trajectories for political engagement. -A Political Economy Analysis (PEA) was conducted to understand the dynamics of political inclusion and exclusion in politics (in the process of finalization).
Area 3: Increased state accountability (through legislative oversight) -Initial meetings were held with leadership of both houses of the Legislature and their Secretariats to foster relationships and identify entry points for technical assistance. -Technical support was agreed with the Joint Legislative Modernization Committee (JLMC) on operationalization of the Legislative Modernization Plan and a working session was held. -Review was initiated of available standing orders and other procedural documents as well as the Open Legislative Index report to identify policy and institutional gaps that will inform design of appropriate interventions in 2025. -The Project contributed to induction training for the legislature on topics of representing constituents interests, explaining the New Election Law and promoting gender equality. -A mapping exercise of CSOs and media groups involved in monitoring the work of the legislature was undertaken to identify partners and beneficiaries for capacity development.
